newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Bank Hapoalim chief blasts Netanyahu policy.
newsitem.headline: Israel Bank Hapoalim chief blasts Netanyahu policy.

text.p: Emanuel Sharon, chairman of Israel's Bank Hapoalim, blasted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's handling of economic policy in an interview published on Friday.
"We are in the midst of a fog that is becoming thicker. Do you know what the economic policy is? I don't know...No one knows," Israel's Maariv daily quoted Sharon as saying.
Netanyahu's spokesman was not immediately available to comment.

Sharon, head of Israel's largest bank, attacked what he said was lack of coordination between Netanyahu, Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel over a Treasury-sponsored capital market reform package.
"The manner of dealing with the report...gave negative signals towards the economy and the way in which economic decisions are reached," Sharon said.

"The fact that the prime minister and finance minister entered the meeting without coordination has no precedent in the Israeli economy...there were also differences of opinion between the governor and the finance minister," Sharon told Maariv.

Netanyahu persuaded ministers at a marathon cabinet meeting this week to delay voting on a key clause in the reform plan that would have imposed taxes on short- and medium-term savings. The move was widely seen as a defeat for Meridor.

Netanyahu this week also broke ranks with central bank head Frenkel, whom he had previously publicly supported, by calling for interest rate cuts. Analysts called the move a political calculation unlikely to alter the bank's monetary stance.
Frenkel for his part on Wednesday reversed his opposition to the savings tax in the reform package. He said he would now support it in hopes of saving the entire reform package.
"An unclear economic policy is not an economic policy," Sharon said. "Only if people believe in the policy is it an economic policy."
